content.text: characterized by macules or small papules after the initiation of drug treatment
MC occurs 5-14d after the initiation of the offending med
or within 1-2d in previously sensitized individuals
; for short courses of tx (e.g., antibiotics), the eruption may appear
: slightly elevated acute phase reactants, mild eosinophilia
Prompt withdrawal of the offending med
Self-limited, localized subcutaneous (or submucosal) swelling resulting from extravasation of fluid into the interstitium
Affects the mucosal tissues of the face, lips, tongue, larynx, hands, feet, & genitalia
Onset in min-hours w/ spontaneous resolution in hours-few days
accompanied w/ other allergic rxn sxs
(urticaria, flushing, pruritis, bronchospasm, stridor, throat tightness, hypotension)
Bradykinin-mediated (e.g., ACEI-induced or hereditary – d/t C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency
If there is no information to suggest an external cause & the patient has isolated angioedema (w/o pruritis or urticaria), then C4 levels & a C1 inhibitor antigenic level should be obtained
: immediate assessment & ongoing airway protection; epi if severe
Edema of the superficial layers of the skin due histamine-related increased vascular permeability
: release of vasodilators (histamine, bradykinin, kallikrein, PGs) form mast cells & basophils of the skin
Triggers: foods, meds, heat or cold, stress, insect bites, environmental, & infection
circumscribed hives or wheals (blanchable, raised, erythematous areas on the skin or mucous membranes)
) may be added if no response to H1 blockers
Drug Reaction w/ Eosinophilia & Systemic Symptoms (DRESS)/Drug-Induced Hypersensitivity Syndrome (DIHS)
: distinct & potentially life-threatening severe ADR characterized by a morbilliform cutaneous eruption w/ fever, LAD, hematologic abnormalities, & multiorgan manifestations
: appears to be mediated by activation of CD4+ & CD8+ T lymphocytes;
most often occurs 2-6wks after medication initiation
: fever, pharyngitis, malaise 2-3d before rash onset
morbilliform exanthem w/ accentuation on face, upper trunk, proximal extremities
•desquamation develops days-weeks after initial eruption; can last several weeks
: hepatitis, tubulointerstitial nephritis, pulmonary sxs (SOB, tachypnea, cough)
exanthema w/ fever, suspicion of drug reaction, hospitalization, LAD, involvement of ≥1 internal organ, & hematologic abnormalities
: can show lymphocytosis, atypical lymphocytosis, eosinophilia, thrombocytopenia
: HAV IgM Ab, HBsAg, HBcAb (IgM), HCV viral RNA
for no response to steroids; plasmapheresis, immunosuppressive drugs are other options
